omahab.description: Single private bridge for platform bundles. No host port publishing for application services; only caddy edge publishes 80/443 and cloudflared uses outbound tunnel.

bundles.name: caddy
bundles.description: Omahab edge reverse proxy. Terminates TLS via Cloudflare DNS-01, routes vanity and .home hostnames to platform services and ONCE proxy (127.0.0.1:8080).

images.caddy: ghcr.io/caddybuilds/caddy-cloudflare@sha256:${CADDY_DIGEST:?pinned digest required - substituted from signed release manifest}

resources.notes: Edge is lightweight; memory scales with number of vhosts and TLS cache.

persistence.description: ACME certificates, OCSP, and Caddy storage

backup.notes: Certificates are re-issuable via DNS-01; backup primarily preserves OCSP and avoids re-issuance storms.

hooks: systemctl reload caddy || docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec caddy caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile || true
restore.notes: Restore volumes then reload Caddy. Certificates will re-issue automatically if missing.

secrets.notes: Caddy itself holds no long-lived secret; Cloudflare DNS-01 token is projected via secret file into caddy env through omahabd-templated Caddyfile (not Docker labels).

oidc.notes: Caddy is not OIDC-protected; it forwards Authorization headers to backends.

exposure.capabilities: Edge itself is not toggled; downstream services declare private/shared/public and Caddy renders route + Tunnel vs DNS-only accordingly.
exposure.notes: No application port is published directly; Caddy owns :80/:443 and ONCE proxy sits on 127.0.0.1:8080 behind Caddy.

bundles.name: pocket-id
bundles.description: Passkey-first OIDC identity provider for all native-OIDC applications. Groups: admins, members, guests.

persistence.description: SQLite or backend data (when not using external Postgres). Encrypted at rest by host.

preHooks: docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec pocket-id /app/backend/pocket-id backup --out /tmp/pocket-id-backup.db || cp /app/backend/data/data.db /tmp/pocket-id-backup.db
backup.notes: Always use application-aware hook before snapshotting the volume; raw volume copy without dump is invalid for restore.

hooks: docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec pocket-id /app/backend/pocket-id restore --in /tmp/pocket-id-backup.db || cp /tmp/pocket-id-backup.db /app/backend/data/data.db
restore.notes: Restore DB file then restart service.

secretFiles.description: Application encryption key projected via file, not env var.

secrets.notes: Upstream supports *_FILE for secrets; omahabd projects via Docker secrets / tmpfs (/run/secrets) with 0400 root ownership.

oidc.notes: Pocket ID IS the provider; other apps consume it. No self-OIDC.

exposure.publicWarning: Pocket ID should never be public without Access gate.
exposure.notes: Private via CNAME -> home A record (Tailscale IP). Shared via Cloudflare Tunnel + Access gate.

bundles.name: forgejo
bundles.description: Canonical Git forge. Private by default. Forgejo is the source of truth; GitHub mirror is read-only via push mirror.

resources.notes: Scales with repo count and LFS; Postgres dominates.

preHooks: docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec forgejo forgejo dump --file /tmp/forgejo_app.zip --type zip || true
backup.notes: Database MUST be dumped via pg_dump; raw volume copy alone is NOT a valid backup. Repos on volume + pgdump together are restorable.

restore.notes: Restore Postgres dump before app start; repos are on forgejo_data volume.

secrets.notes: Prefer *_FILE secrets; fallback env only where upstream lacks file support. Secrets never appear in labels/logs.

oidc.notes: Forgejo native OIDC client toward Pocket ID. Edge auth not used to avoid breaking API/mobile clients.

exposure.notes: Private = DNS-only -> Tailscale IP. Shared/Public via Tunnel (shared adds Access gate). Warn before making unauthenticated Forgejo public.

update.notes: Forgejo runs DB migrations on start; rollback restores previous DB dump.

bundles.name: woodpecker
bundles.description: CI for Forgejo. Single runner family; isolated server + agent. Forgejo Actions disabled to avoid dual pipeline systems.

persistence.description: Woodpecker server state (if non-Postgres) - backup only when used

backup.notes: Consistent Postgres dump required; do not snapshot live DB files alone.

secrets.notes: Woodpecker supports secret files for Forgejo OAuth and agent GRPC secret; prefer files over env.

oidc.notes: Auth delegated to Forgejo; Pocket ID is not Woodpecker's direct IdP. Users authenticate via Forgejo which itself uses Pocket ID.

exposure.notes: Woodpecker UI is private/shared only; public CI UI is discouraged.

bundles.name: hermes
bundles.description: Default AI assistant backend and project bots. Stable profile 'default' mapped to user-chosen display name (default AI). Remote gateway for WebSocket/JSON-RPC.

resources.notes: Memory scales with conversation history and tool use; embedding worker is SEPARATE failure domain (see worker).

persistence.description: Hermes profiles, bot definitions, conversations, tool approvals

backup.notes: Database dump is authoritative; vector/index derived data follows Paperless backup policy, not dumped here.

secrets.notes: Model gateway credentials are supplied via LiteLLM virtual keys, not upstream provider tokens directly to Hermes.

oidc.notes: Hermes web and API authenticate via Pocket ID OIDC; bot scopes isolated per project.

exposure.notes: Default assistant at ai.<domain> via Pocket ID. Private tailnet-only by default; shared via Tunnel+Access.

bundles.name: immich
bundles.description: Private photo and video management. Mobile clients via Pocket ID / native auth; machine-learning via separate Immich ML container (isolated failure boundary).

resources.notes: Immich ML is CPU-heavy; arm64 uses smaller model footprint. Disk scales with media library under /srv/omahab/apps/immich/library.

preHooks: docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec immich-server immich backup --out /tmp/immich_library_manifest.json || echo 'library manifest hook placeholder'
backup.notes: Per https://docs.immich.app/administration/backup-and-restore/ : database dump + upload folder are both required and must be consistent. Raw DB files alone are invalid.

restore.notes: Restore DB dump, then restore library files, then restart. Verify with `immich admin` check.

secrets.notes: Immich supports *_FILE for DB password; other secrets via env files projected from omahabd.

oidc.notes: Immich native OIDC toward Pocket ID. Mobile clients use OIDC tokens; fallback local auth disabled by default.

exposure.notes: Private recommended; shared via Access gate protects album links. Public not recommended for private media.

update.notes: Immich requires matching server + ML image versions from same release; both pinned together.

bundles.name: paperless-ngx
bundles.description: Document management system of record. REST API for retrieval. Supports native OIDC and local embedding indexing via separate worker (failure-isolated).

resources.notes: Disk scales with document store (/srv/omahab/apps/paperless). Gotenberg+Tika are CPU bursts during ingestion.

preHooks: docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec paperless document_exporter --no-progress --zip /tmp/paperless_export.zip || docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec paperless python3 manage.py document_exporter /tmp/paperless_export --zip --no-progress || true
backup.notes: Consistent DB dump + media/data volume snapshot required; raw DB files alone are invalid. document_exporter provides portable fallback.

hooks: docker compose -f {{.ComposeFile}} exec paperless python3 manage.py document_importer /tmp/paperless_export --no-progress || rsync -a /backups/paperless/media/ /srv/omahab/apps/paperless/media/

secrets.notes: Paperless supports PAPERLESS_*_FILE for file-based secrets; omahabd projects via /run/secrets tmpfs.

oidc.notes: Paperless native OIDC toward Pocket ID; local search index follows Paperless permissions.

exposure.notes: Documents are private by default; shared requires Access gate.

backup.notes: Meilisearch index can be rebuilt from DB+data volume; only DB and data volume are authoritative backups.
